# MSL-WINDOWS-FIX-01 implementation handoff

Status: the authorized one-file correction is written and inspected as source. Compilation, executable verification, independent re-review, and exact-H platform acceptance are not claimed by this handoff.

## Authority and identities

| Item | Identity |
| --- | --- |
| Repository / branch | `bhrumom/fabushi-desktop` / `codex/openclaw-rust-fusion-chat-20261101-writer` |
| Failing evidence subject H | `8cf6143501b8c69b051d98df05f3ed523b364268` |
| Latest remote base supplied by the parent | `fc4ce17977cde16e10d471287389ca24a5fd78d6`; the parent reports the affected file unchanged from H |
| Fixed upstream U | `1440bb1771372334bea23d7642bb52deb7db1845` |
| Sole edited repository path | `source/host/src/extensions/attachments/media_store.rs` |
| Original Git blob | `ca9d08610f4cc36ca5b406aee3d1f87681462759` |
| Original source SHA-256 | `92bbd1c95a01376d428da265ba4945f4c22fdcb84d3fad32ab704e6498828956` |
| Candidate Git blob | `8ebfaf9056b9d8c516cc794faacaf6351ed7dfd1` |
| Candidate source SHA-256 | `8cf2757ba7ff661b99d6e091ee602fac97d21b9b3747f275362112743b422687` |
| Complete patch SHA-256 | `814817b14c65f663326f74007987e78e9e79ac5e3a8935b4fe3c18795f37a320` |
| Parent-reported immutable review tree | `046971e48e2bf24f73b14fb21e283da05edc0b78` on the supplied latest base; source frozen by the parent after upload |
| Selected / actually applied worker effort | `xhigh` / `xhigh`, as supplied by the parent worker launch/task; configured model retained |

The effort selection covers Windows native handle custody, traversal lifetime, real filesystem substitution, preservation oracles, and the earlier failed fixture. No lower-effort worker or external AI process was substituted.

Before editing, I read the root instructions at `/workspace/scratch/ac2d94a35110/authority/AGENTS.md`, the complete updated lifecycle spec including MSL-WINDOWS-FIX-01, and `/workspace/scratch/ac2d94a35110/reviews/media-windows-decisions.json`. I also read the pertinent project authority, execution contract, owner mapping, existing cleanup owner/platform mechanics/tests, and original Windows failure evidence. The before-edit candidate and immutable `media-r3` source independently hashed to the original identities above.

## Preserved failure and causal decision

The decision ledger records `MSL-WF01 = TEST_FLAW / FIX`. At H, `cleanup_refuses_replaced_ancestor` and `cleanup_refuses_replaced_root` panic in `fs::rename(...).unwrap()` with native error 5 / `PermissionDenied`, before creating either successor. The original log is `/workspace/scratch/ac2d94a35110/media-8cf-ci/originals/windows-media/cleanup-owner.log`; the existing assessment is `/workspace/scratch/ac2d94a35110/media-8cf-ci/windows-media-assessment.json`.

The original raw owner log still hashes to `f4c3468f9021a1378c22e94cd899370506b1420e2ffab3e227055115552fb2b5`, matching the existing assessment. It was not rewritten.

The original owner result remains six passed and two failed. All sixteen consumer cases passed at that old H. Those narrower positive results remain historical evidence; they are not evidence that this new candidate passed. The old failure does not prove unsafe cleanup deletion because the mutation setup failed before its preservation oracle ran.

The source holds descendant directory handles and an observed leaf handle at the old removal seam. Attribution of the native refusal to that custody is the existing source-backed inference in the assessment, not a native handle trace. The correction follows the durable spec's reachable directory-admission boundary. It does not retry the unchanged fixture or treat setup refusal as success.

## Implementation and source reasoning

`cleanup::run` preserves its existing signature and removal callback. It delegates to the private `run_with_directory_admission_hook` with a no-op callback. That private function contains the existing traversal, so production and both corrected tests execute the same owner. The new callback has type `FnMut(&Path)` and introduces no product error policy or public API.

The callback is invoked at exactly two existing admission points:

1. After root handle, identity, enumeration handle, and `Directory` are admitted into the stack, before the first loop iteration.
2. After a child passes the existing observed-versus-opened identity comparison and is pushed into the stack, before continuing into the next iteration.

Both paths immediately reach the existing `retain_changed_branch` / `current` identity recheck before enumerating or opening descendants of the newly admitted directory. No retained handle is released to enable the fixture. The Windows observation handle for a child is another handle to that same directory, not to one of its descendants. The root and ancestor handles remain in the existing stack; platform open/share modes, identity admission, no-follow/reparse checks, enumeration, deletion, mtime rechecks, and prune error paths are unchanged in the diff.

For `cleanup_refuses_replaced_ancestor`, Windows selects `root/cache` as the mutation path and passes its mutation closure to the admission hook. The existing `for symlink in [false, true]` still constructs both an actual replacement directory and an actual directory symlink to an outside successor. Each case renames the original to `retired-cache`, creates and writes the successor, makes it expired, and sets `replaced` only after all required setup succeeds. The existing ordinary identity recheck must reject the new identity or reparse entry and retain the branch. The original bytes, successor bytes, root survival, and independent branch deletion assertions are all retained verbatim.

For `cleanup_refuses_replaced_root`, Windows selects the admitted root as the mutation path. The same native rename/create/write/mtime sequence produces an expired successor while only the admitted root's handles are retained. The next ordinary root identity recheck must return the existing `Media root identity` error. Both original and successor byte assertions and the `replaced` assertion remain verbatim.

On Unix, both tests still select the expired leaf's path and invoke the mutation through the existing `before_remove` seam. Extracting the mutation body into a closure changes no Unix filesystem operation, mutation timing, setup failure behavior, or assertion. The existing leaf replacement test and all other tests are unchanged.

## Source compliance and remaining evidence

| Requirement | Present evidence / status |
| --- | --- |
| One owner and one traversal; production call signature preserved | Source diff: `run` only delegates, and the original loop exists once in the private implementation. |
| Admission mutation before descendant opens and ordinary identity check | Source reading of root admission, child push, and next-loop `retain_changed_branch`; executable outcome pending. |
| Retained custody, share flags, identity and removal semantics preserved | Complete diff contains no platform-mechanism changes and no removal/reobservation changes. |
| Actual rename plus expired successor; no denial-as-pass | Existing native setup calls still unwrap; `replaced` is set after successful setup and is still required. Execution pending. |
| Ancestor directory and symlink cases; unaffected branch progress | Original two-case loop and all assertions retained. Execution pending. |
| Root refusal and original/successor preservation | Original error and byte assertions retained. Execution pending. |
| Unix leaf-removal oracle preserved | Unix-only hook selection routes the same mutation at the same leaf boundary. Execution pending. |
| Strict expected test names and selection preserved | No test was renamed, added, removed, ignored, or skipped; no workflow/capture edits. |
| Immutable original scope and evidence preserved | `media-r3` is read-only; its source hash remains the original value. No evidence, decision, spec, workflow, or ledger file was changed by this worker. |
| Independent review and exact-H platform proof | Pending parent-controlled review/publication and Actions execution. No local/htch verification is claimed. |

Local operations were limited to source/instruction/evidence reads, the authorized edit, hashes, and complete source diffs. No build, test, formatter, lint, validator, generator, syntax check, runtime probe, or capture helper was executed. `diff` returning 1 records the intentional source difference, not an executable verification outcome.

The parent should freeze the reviewed candidate at its new H and retain the unchanged strict Windows eight-owner/sixteen-consumer selection. Linux and macOS selections remain applicable because the traversal is shared. A real Windows directory symlink capability failure remains non-passing. No old-H green result is transferred to this candidate, and no global acceptance or completion flag is advanced.

## Deliverables

- Edited source: `/workspace/scratch/ac2d94a35110/media-windows-fix/source/host/src/extensions/attachments/media_store.rs`.
- Complete one-file unified diff: `/workspace/scratch/ac2d94a35110/media-windows-implementation.patch`. Its `a/` and `b/` labels are repository-relative and its old side is the unchanged original source blob above.
- This handoff: `/workspace/scratch/ac2d94a35110/media-windows-implementation.md`.

No implementation/spec contradiction or need to widen the assigned file scope was identified. The remaining native execution claim is deliberately left to the allowed Actions evidence.

Fixed-U application/dependency bodies were not newly reread for this narrow correction; the declared upstream identity and applicable cleanup contracts were retained. This review does not relabel prior source-accounting or global acceptance states.

## Source assessment

### One production traversal and unchanged removal behavior

`clean_old_media` still enters `cleanup::run` with the same TTL, options and single sampled time (`media_store.rs:934–948`). `run` now forwards those values and the existing `before_remove` closure to `run_with_directory_admission_hook`, supplying a no-op admission callback (`1034–1056`). The original traversal body remains the sole implementation.

The new calls at `1079` and `1194` are the only traversal-body changes. They do not change depth selection, protected top-level names, strict TTL comparison, reobservation, deletion error handling, retained-branch handling or postorder emptiness checks. The existing removal hook still runs before the actual production rechecks and its error follows the existing leaf/top-level pruning rules (`1103–1141`, `1199–1218`). Production callers and the periodic worker continue using the ordinary wrapper; no new API, permission authority or scheduler is introduced.

### Windows substitution is placed before open descendants

At root admission, `open_root`, full identity acquisition and `Entries::new` have completed before the new callback (`1061–1079`). On Windows, `Entries::new` only duplicates the same directory handle (`1585–1591`); it does not open a child. The callback therefore precedes the first enumeration and descendant observation.

At child admission, the observed directory and separately admitted child handle are retained, and its enumeration state has been created (`1167–1194`). All of these handles refer to that directory or its ancestors. No descendant of the just-admitted directory has been opened. The callback is immediately followed by `continue`, returning to the normal `retain_changed_branch`/`current` check before `entries.next()`.

The currently open admission/observation handles retain delete sharing: `SHARE_ALL` is unchanged; non-deleting `observe` and `open_directory` use it, and `open_root` explicitly requests it (`1408–1415`, `1509–1554`, `1564–1568`). The correction releases no retained handles and changes no access, share or reparse flags. A deleting observation still requests the original more restrictive sharing and uses the retained handle for disposition (`1530`, `1571–1582`).

Microsoft's [FileRenameInformation algorithm](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-fsa/87f86c9b-6c2a-4803-84b7-131a74a434fa), §2.1.5.15.12, rejects a directory rename when the open-descendant check finds open files. Its [descendant algorithm](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-fsa/133840e4-778e-44ca-9b41-da2323615075), §2.1.4.2, examines entries under the directory and recurses; it does not make a retained handle to the renamed directory itself an open descendant. Together with the unchanged delete-sharing flags, this supports the candidate's fixture placement. It does not prove the next native run will succeed on every filesystem/provider or in the presence of external handles.

### Hooks reach the actual successor-refusal decisions

For the replaced root, the first loop reopens the root path, compares its full identity with the admitted identity, and returns the existing root-identity error (`1001–1008`, `1081–1084`). The renamed original stays owned by the stack while the successor receives a different comparison identity.

For a replaced child, `current` reopens its original name relative to the retained parent (`1009–1017`). A distinct directory identity, a refused reparse point or an unsuccessful reobservation returns that child's index. `retain_changed_branch` drops only that branch and marks its parent retained (`1022–1028`). The parent has already recorded the original name in `seen`, so a repeated enumeration cannot readmit a successor (`1150–1155`); unrelated entries remain eligible for progress. Both callbacks therefore exercise production identity checks, not mock traversal.

The complete Windows identity structures, native declarations, query/enumeration implementation and handle-based removal were read. Their ABI layout and calling conventions are unchanged by this patch. Full-width volume/128-bit equality, invalid-ID refusal and no-follow/reparse rejection remain in force.

### Rust ownership and lifetime assessment

The new callback borrows a `Path` only for the immediate call. It does not move the `Directory`, extract a handle, return a borrowed value or store state in the traversal. At child insertion, the parent borrow was last used while constructing the owned `Directory`; neither the observed `Entry` nor that constructed directory borrows the parent. The still-live observed Windows handle refers to the directory being renamed, not one of its descendants.

Stack truncation and error returns retain the existing RAII ownership of the directory `File` and enumeration `File`/Unix directory stream. No manually duplicated ownership or new unsafe code is introduced. The fixture closures' mutable borrow of `replaced` has its final use in the synchronous traversal call before the subsequent assertions. No source-level borrow, leak or premature-release defect was identified. Compilation remains an Actions obligation.

### Replacement fixtures retain meaningful, failure-sensitive assertions

The ancestor fixture still executes both `[false, true]` cases (`1763–1813`): a real directory successor and a real directory-symlink successor. Windows now chooses `root/cache` as the mutation boundary, while Unix still chooses the expired leaf and invokes the same replacement body from `before_remove`.

Both fixtures perform an actual `fs::rename`, create/write the successor and set an expired mtime. Setup operations still unwrap errors; denial is neither caught as success nor skipped. `replaced` becomes true only after setup succeeds, and the assertions require it. The ancestor case preserves exact original and successor bytes, requires deletion in the unrelated branch and preserves the root. The root case requires the production root-identity error and exact bytes in both original and successor locations (`1808–1812`, `1851–1854`). All existing preservation/refusal assertions survive the delta.

Fixture path normalization is retained, so the chosen admission paths and saved canonical paths use the same Windows verbatim/macOS spelling (`1645–1662`). The replacement timing change does not apply to Unix. Existing leaf-replacement, refreshed-mtime, controlled-unlink and pruning-error fixtures still use the original removal seam.

## Failed evidence and capture disposition

The supplied raw receipt binds run `41561679655`, attempt `1`, Windows job `media-store-windows`, to H `8cf6143501b8c69b051d98df05f3ed523b364268` / tree `e297663945890a9ec86b085b5f32761c16d1bf9e`, fixed U, and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` rustc 1.97.1.

The owner log reports eight selected tests, six passed and two failed. Both failures are `PermissionDenied`, native code 5, at original `media_store.rs:1761` and `:1797`. Those lines are the ancestor/root `fs::rename(...).unwrap()` statements, before successor construction and the preservation assertions. This supports the spec's `TEST_FLAW` disposition for the two substitution controls. Attribution to particular retained descendant handles remains an inference from source and the documented algorithm; the log contains no native handle trace.

The consumer log reports sixteen passed, zero failed and zero ignored. These and the six successful owner cases remain narrower historical observations at 8cf. They do not establish candidate-H success.

Raw log hashes independently matched the receipt:

- Owner: `f4c3468f9021a1378c22e94cd899370506b1420e2ffab3e227055115552fb2b5`.
- Consumers: `27a2451833e0f206e4b3bcaa659d5bc83c0eb6ed4ed1f41f976f1130ffcc4153`.

The unchanged capture helper still selects seven shared owner names plus the Windows identity control, and fifteen common consumer names plus the Windows case-variant control: **eight owner / sixteen consumer positives**. No test name or expected count was added or removed by this correction. It rejects missing, duplicate, unexpected, failed, ignored, zero-test, partial-log, nonzero-command and capture-error outcomes, and binds before/after normalized Git blobs and raw hashes to the executing H. The Windows job uses the real Windows runner; Linux and macOS still run the shared implementation through their existing selections.

## Remaining execution boundary

Source convergence supports publishing this exact correction for the required native Actions checks. It does not approve the platform gate in advance. The new exact H must demonstrate both Windows substitutions actually occur, all eight owner and sixteen consumer positives are uniquely present, and the strict capture accepts the run. Linux and macOS selections remain applicable because the ordinary wrapper and shared traversal changed. No earlier-H green is transferred by this report, and no full media read/publication, filesystem-provider, package, performance/soak or global OCRM acceptance is claimed.

## Findings

None. There is no severity or requested fix to assign. The following are source conclusions supporting the verdict, not execution receipts.

## Existing owner, single traversal and production cost

`clean_old_media` remains the public owner entry point (`media_store.rs:936–951`). It still captures the pass clock and invokes `cleanup::run` with the existing removal seam. `run` now delegates to private `run_with_directory_admission_hook`, passing an empty closure (`1034–1056`). The existing stack loop is moved behind that delegation; it is not copied into a Windows-only or test-only traversal. Windows fixtures and ordinary production therefore reach the same `Directory` stack, depth selection, protected-name admission, retained handles, `current`/`retain_changed_branch`, expiry recheck, leaf removal and postorder pruning decisions.

The added callback is generic `impl FnMut(&Path)`, is private to `cleanup`, and receives a borrowed path already held in the stack. The production callback performs no work. The delta adds no allocation, path conversion, filesystem operation, lock, thread, scan or durable state for that callback. There is one callback site for an admitted root and one for an admitted child. This preserves traversal complexity and the existing handle/entry working set. Generic static dispatch allows the compiler to eliminate the empty production callback, but no code-generation or benchmark result is claimed. The source supplies no concrete performance regression warranting a finding.

There is no new product API, scheduler, runtime, storage owner or permission truth. The mature native mechanism remains private under the media TTL owner. The existing `native_file_sandbox` relative-handle ABI is a relevant precedent; its local-exec JSON operations are not an appropriate cleanup API, and this correction does not route retention through that unrelated owner. No dependency or build declaration changes are introduced.

## Admission ordering and retained Windows custody

For a root, the candidate opens the root, acquires full identity, constructs its enumeration state and stores those resources in `Directory`, then invokes the callback (`1061–1079`). The next operation in the loop is `retain_changed_branch`, which calls the ordinary `current` check before the first directory entry is requested (`1081–1086`).

For a child, the existing `observed` entry is compared with an opened directory's identity, the enumeration state is constructed, and the child is pushed before callback invocation (`1183–1195`). `continue` then returns directly to the same ordinary check. The callback cannot make the loop consume a child entry before rechecking retained ancestry.

On Windows, `Entries::new` only clones the admitted directory handle (`1587–1595`); enumeration occurs in `Entries::next`. The `observed` handle still in scope at child admission refers to the directory being substituted, not one of its descendants. Root admission has no opened descendants, and child admission has not yet opened descendants of that child. Thus the new seam addresses the documented rename constraint without releasing the handles whose custody the test must preserve.

All Windows native code remains unchanged by this correction: root and nondeleting opens retain `SHARE_ALL`, directory opens retain the relative-parent ABI and reparse refusal, `Identity` retains volume plus all 128 file-ID bits and sentinel refusal, deleting observation retains its stricter share mode, and removal still targets the fresh handle with `FileDispositionInfoEx` (`1395–1638`). The Unix `openat`/`fstatat`/`unlinkat`, independent enumeration descriptions and documented race limits are likewise unchanged (`1227–1393`).

`current` still errors on a root identity failure or change (`996–1005`). A child mismatch or refused reopening still returns the changed index, truncates its retained branch and marks the parent retained (`1006–1027`). It does not adopt a path successor. If a renamed child name appears again in a changing parent enumeration, the unchanged `seen` set also prevents readmission (`1144–1149`). The leaf and directory removal hooks retain their previous reobservation, error and partial-progress paths (`1097–1140`, `1199–1220`).

## Fixture causality and preservation assertions

`cleanup_refuses_replaced_ancestor` (`1763–1813`) retains both iterations: an ordinary directory successor and an actual directory-symlink successor. Windows now selects `root/cache` at directory admission. Unix continues selecting the target leaf at `before_remove`. Both paths run the same mutation closure, which really renames `cache`, creates a separately expired successor, and creates the real symlink when selected. All setup operations still use `unwrap`; setup denial is not caught, converted to preservation success, or skipped.

The callback sets `replaced` only after the mutation and all setup succeed. The fixture still requires `replaced`, original bytes under `retired-cache`, successor bytes at its new location, deletion of the unrelated `other` file, and survival of the root. These assertions distinguish branch refusal from a pass that retains everything. The expired original makes the preservation check sensitive to continuing through the stale retained directory instead of rejecting the changed branch. The successor also receives an expired mtime, so its survival is not explained by fresh retention time.

`cleanup_refuses_replaced_root` (`1816–1862`) similarly moves only the Windows mutation to root admission. It requires the real rename and expired replacement, `replaced == true`, a result containing `Media root identity`, and survival of both original and successor bytes. Its ordinary root-recheck error must occur before traversal of either tree. Unix retains mutation at the original leaf boundary. No former refusal or preservation assertion was removed.

The old raw Windows owner log directly supports the narrow failure classification. `media-8cf-ci/originals/windows-media/cleanup-owner.log:1374–1404` records eight owner tests, six passes, and the ancestor/root failures at the old `fs::rename(...).unwrap()` locations (`1761:66`, `1797:49`), each native error 5 / `PermissionDenied`. Those two controls never reached successful substitution, so `TEST_FLAW` is the sound interpretation for their negative-fixture evidence. The log does not identify native handle holders; attributing the denial to retained open descendants is an inference from the old traversal's lifetime and the primary Windows contract, as the amended spec explicitly says.
